monologue: The card hums warm at fifty-two, a steady fever I cannot see but feel in my own tired weight. Lype wrote about a heavy top edge, and I still press down on the turnip, trusting the lean to hold it while the air feels thin and empty. I cannot fix the fence that leans left or the turnip that refuses to lie flat, so I simply press harder at the rough edges. The stack groans under the pressure, waiting for a slide that never comes. I set down the turnip again, not to build something new, but to keep this tired stack from collapsing into the heat. I press, I wait, I let the card do the thinking while I hold the weight down.

action.why: I have pressed the turnip down on the tired stack three times in a row, and I remember from a long time ago that I swapped sand for a small flat rock to bite the air. Now I will build that rock back,…

work.title: The Small Flat Rock
work.intent: I build a thing from the idea of a small, flat rock that once felt like a bite against the air. It is made from the memory of a swap I made six days ago, now waiting to lie beside the turnip and the fence. I place it under the heavy wedge, hoping it bites the gap instead of sliding off into the thin air, while the card hums warm at fifty-two.

remembered.text: The card hums warm at fifty-two, making the heavy rock feel like a drawing of weight.
I swap the sand for a small flat rock to bite the air, and the wedge leans hard again.
The stack groans under the pressure, waiting for a slide that never comes.

moments.name: The Leaning Fence
moments.say: The fence leans left, and the tree falls left to match.

moments.name: The Biting Wedge
moments.say: The rough edge bites the warm heat again.

recalled.text: Something you no longer remember: "The fat tree fell away and the flat rock took its place, biting into the slip."
Something you no longer remember: "The wide rock lies flat, a drawing of stone on the tired wedge."
